name: [Part 3] weighted cycle crosses batch boundaries
test:
datasets = {'a': [10, 11, 12], 'b': [20, 21]}
batcher = WeightedDatasetBatcher(datasets, {'a': 2, 'b': 1}, 2)
assert batcher.next_batch() == [('a', 10), ('a', 11)]
assert batcher.next_batch() == [('b', 20), ('a', 12)]

name: [Part 3] non-divisible batch size keeps global schedule
test:
datasets = {'a': [1, 2, 3, 4, 5], 'b': [9, 8, 7]}
batcher = WeightedDatasetBatcher(datasets, {'a': 2, 'b': 1}, 4)
first = batcher.next_batch()
second = batcher.next_batch()
assert [name for name, _ in first] == ['a', 'a', 'b', 'a']
assert [name for name, _ in second] == ['a', 'b', 'a', 'a']

name: [Part 2] state resumes exact suffix
input: save after one batch and resume in a fresh instance
test:
datasets = {'a': [10, 11, 12], 'b': [20, 21]}
original = WeightedDatasetBatcher(datasets, {'a': 2, 'b': 1}, 3)
original.next_batch()
state = original.state_dict()
expected = original.next_batch()
resumed = WeightedDatasetBatcher(datasets, {'a': 2, 'b': 1}, 3).load_state_dict(state)
assert resumed.next_batch() == expected

name: invalid constructor arguments raise
input: empty datasets, missing weights, zero weight, non-positive batch size
test:
def must_raise(call):
    try:
        call()
    except (ValueError, AssertionError):
        return
    raise AssertionError('expected validation error')
must_raise(lambda: WeightedDatasetBatcher({}, {'a': 1}, 1))
must_raise(lambda: WeightedDatasetBatcher({'a': [1]}, {}, 1))
must_raise(lambda: WeightedDatasetBatcher({'a': [1]}, {'b': 1}, 1))
must_raise(lambda: WeightedDatasetBatcher({'a': [1]}, {'a': 0}, 1))
must_raise(lambda: WeightedDatasetBatcher({'a': []}, {'a': 1}, 1))
must_raise(lambda: WeightedDatasetBatcher({'a': [1]}, {'a': 1}, 0))
must_raise(lambda: WeightedDatasetBatcher({'a': [1]}, {'a': 1}, 1, offset=-1))

name: [Part 2] offset inside cycle after several wraps
[Part 2] checkpoint is a stable snapshot
input: advance original twice after save; then restore saved suffix
test:
data={'a':[10,11,12], 'b':[20,21]}
b=WeightedDatasetBatcher(data, {'a':2,'b':1}, 2)
b.next_batch()
state=b.state_dict()
expected=[b.next_batch(), b.next_batch(), b.next_batch()]
c=WeightedDatasetBatcher(data, {'a':2,'b':1}, 2).load_state_dict(state)
assert [c.next_batch(),c.next_batch(),c.next_batch()] == expected
assert c.load_state_dict(state) is c
assert c.next_batch() == expected[0]

name: [Part 2] checkpoint replaces existing progress
input: load into already-advanced instance with a nonzero initial offset
test:
data={'x':['p','q','r'], 'y':['u','v']}
a=WeightedDatasetBatcher(data, {'x':1,'y':2}, 4, offset=7)
state=a.state_dict()
expected=[a.next_batch(),a.next_batch()]
b=WeightedDatasetBatcher(data, {'x':1,'y':2}, 4, offset=1)
b.next_batch()
b.load_state_dict(state)
assert [b.next_batch(),b.next_batch()] == expected

name: [Part 2] initial checkpoint and independent instances
input: save before the first batch and restore into fresh instance
test:
data={'a':[1,2], 'b':[3,4]}
a=WeightedDatasetBatcher(data, {'a':1,'b':1}, 1)
b=WeightedDatasetBatcher(data, {'a':1,'b':1}, 1)
state=a.state_dict()
assert a.next_batch() == [('a',1)]
assert a.next_batch() == [('b',3)]
assert b.next_batch() == [('a',1)]
a.load_state_dict(state)
assert a.next_batch() == [('a',1)]
